source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Electrical, p.6Y-14

procedures.title: Indicator lamp / initial field excitation circuit: test
steps: Step 2: move the test lamp's ground lead to connect across connector terminals "F" and "4".
If it lights, the regulator has an open circuit or the relay is stuck closed; repair per Service Operations.
If it stays dark, the fault is in the "F"-to-"F" wire or the field windings; go to step 3.
Step 3: move the lamp lead from the connector "F" terminal to the Delcotron "F" terminal.
If it lights, the wire between the "F" terminals is open; fix it. If dark, the Delcotron field is open; repair per Service Operations.

If the lamp stays on or the ammeter shows discharge, suspect: a loose drive belt (adjust), a bad field relay (test and adjust), a bad Delcotron (output test), an open parallel resistance wire at normal idle (or, on ammeter cars, an open field excitation wire to the "ACC" terminal), or, with the switch off, a shorted positive diode.

procedures.title: Field circuit resistance wire: check
steps: Connect a test lamp from harness connector terminal "4" to ground (see figure 11c, step 1, in the manual).
Turn ignition ON and watch the test lamp.
Lamp lights: resistance wire is good.
Lamp dark: the resistor is open. (The dash lamp also stays dark in this test because the two bulbs in series draw too little current.)
notes: The resistance wire is part of the ignition harness and cannot be soldered; repair it with a crimp-type connector.

procedures.title: Field relay: check and adjust
steps: Connect a voltmeter from regulator No. 2 terminal to ground (see figure 12c in the manual).
Run the engine at fast idle (1500 to 2000 rpm) and read the voltmeter.
If it reads zero at the regulator, check the circuit from regulator No. 2 terminal to the Delcotron "R" terminal.
